> AGENT

You're right, and it's worse than a style nit. Two findings:

1. **`LoadChildrenFn` is dead code** — it's referenced only in its own definition and one doc-link; nothing in the core takes or stores it. The agent copied it verbatim from spec §5.1, which is itself self-contradictory (§5.1 says the callback is "registered in the adapter layer, not in Props," but §5.4 step 3 says the adapter "calls `load_children(key)` **prop**").
2. **`Rc` violates the workspace convention** — `Callback<T>` wraps `Arc<T>` and every sibling notification (`on_selection_change`, `on_expanded_change`, `on_reorder`) is `Option<Callback<dyn Fn(...) + Send + Sync>>`, fired from the effect's closure. `Rc` isn't `Send + Sync`, which the Service's `StoredValue`/`Signal` storage requires.

The **best outcome** is to make lazy-load mirror its three siblings exactly: a real `on_load_children` Prop of type `Callback<dyn Fn(Key) + Send + Sync>`, fired by the `Effect::LoadChildren` closure (key captured, like `on_reorder`). That deletes the `Rc` alias **and** the transient `pending_load` field, and resolves the spec's internal inconsistency. Let me map the exact touch points before changing anything.

1420	/// split (the load is needed before any echo can produce children) and even when

1743	
1744	## 5. Variant: Lazy Loading
1745	
1746	`TreeView` supports lazy loading of child nodes for large or server-driven
1747	hierarchies. When a `NotLoaded` node is first expanded, the machine emits the
1748	typed `Effect::LoadChildren` and records the requesting key in
1749	`Context::pending_load`; the adapter reads that key and invokes its
1750	adapter-registered load callback.
1751	
1752	> **Effect, not Event.** Adapter notifications in this machine are typed
1753	> `Effect`s (the same convention as `ScrollFocusedIntoView`, `SelectionChange`,
1754	> `ExpandedChange`, `Reorder`). Because `Machine::Effect` must be `Copy`, the key
1755	> cannot ride on the effect variant; it travels in the transient
1756	> `Context::pending_load` field, which the adapter reads when the effect fires
1757	> (mirroring how `ScrollFocusedIntoView` reads `Context::focused_node`).
1758	
1759	### 5.1 Additional Props
1760	
1761	```rust,no_check
1762	/// The load_children callback is registered in the adapter layer, not in Props.
1763	/// When provided, nodes without pre-loaded children will trigger lazy loading on expand.
1764	/// The adapter observes `Effect::LoadChildren` and calls the user-provided callback
1765	/// with `Context::pending_load`.
1766	```
1767	
1768	```rust,no_check
1769	/// Type alias for the lazy-load callback.
1770	/// The adapter calls this with the parent node's key (read from
1771	/// `Context::pending_load`) when `Effect::LoadChildren` fires.
1772	/// The callback should eventually send a `ChildrenLoaded` event back to the machine.
1773	/// Uses `Rc` so the adapter can clone it into event handler closures.
1774	pub type LoadChildrenFn = alloc::rc::Rc<dyn Fn(Key)>;
1775	```
1776	
1777	### 5.2 Additional Effect, Events, and Context
1778	
1779	```rust,no_check
1780	/// Added to the TreeView `Effect` enum (typed, `Copy`).
1781	/// Emitted when a `NotLoaded` node is first expanded. The adapter reads
1782	/// `Context::pending_load` for the key whose children to fetch.
1783	LoadChildren,
1784	```
1785	
1786	```rust,no_check
1787	/// Added to the TreeView `Context`.
1788	/// Set to `Some(key)` when `Effect::LoadChildren` is emitted; cleared once the
1789	/// load settles (`ChildrenLoaded`/`LoadError`).
1790	pub pending_load: Option<Key>,
1791	```
1792	
1793	```rust,no_check
1794	/// Added to the TreeView `Event` enum.
1795	/// Sent by the consumer (via the adapter callback) when lazy-loaded children
1796	/// arrive. `children` are `TreeItemConfig`s — the public construction type for
1797	/// `TreeCollection` — which the machine splices in under `parent` and rebuilds
1798	/// the collection from (there is no public `Node<T>` constructor, and
1799	/// `TreeItem` does not implement `CollectionItem`, so a config payload is the
1800	/// cleanest insertion path).
1801	ChildrenLoaded {
1802	    /// The parent node key.
1803	    parent: Key,
1804	    /// The loaded children configurations, inserted under `parent`.
1805	    children: Vec<TreeItemConfig<TreeItem>>,
1806	},
1807	/// Sent by the consumer when a lazy load fails for `key`; the machine marks the
1808	/// node `Error` so adapters can show a retry affordance.
1809	LoadError(Key),
1810	```
1811	
1812	### 5.3 Additional Node State
1813	
1814	```rust
1815	/// Per-node lazy-load status.
1816	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
1817	pub enum NodeLoadState {
1818	    /// Children are present in the collection.
1819	    Loaded,
1820	    /// Children are being fetched (loading indicator shown).
1821	    Loading,
1822	    /// Load failed — adapter may show retry affordance.
1823	    Error,
1824	    /// Children have not been requested yet (initial state for lazy nodes).
1825	    NotLoaded,
1826	}
1827	```
1828	
1829	The `tree_view::Context` tracks `load_state: BTreeMap<Key, NodeLoadState>`,
1830	seeded at init (and reseeded on `SyncProps` whenever the data source changes): a
1831	branch advertising the `TreeItem::has_children` affordance but with no children
1832	actually loaded is `NotLoaded`; every other node is `Loaded`. A node being
1833	`Loading` advertises `aria-busy="true"` and `data-ars-loading` on its
1834	branch/leaf element so adapters can render the loading affordance.
1835	
1836	### 5.4 Behavior
1837	
1838	1. User expands a node whose `load_state` is `NotLoaded`.
1839	2. The machine sets `load_state[key] = Loading`, sets `pending_load = Some(key)`,
1840	   and emits `Effect::LoadChildren` (in addition to the normal expand plan).
1841	3. The adapter reads `Context::pending_load` and calls its registered
1842	   `load_children` callback. The consumer fetches data asynchronously.
1843	4. Consumer sends `ChildrenLoaded { parent, children }` when data arrives.
1844	5. The machine splices the children in under `parent`, rebuilds the collection,
1845	   reseeds `load_state` (so `parent` becomes `Loaded`), and clears
1846	   `pending_load`.
1847	6. If loading fails, the consumer sends `LoadError(key)`; the machine sets
1848	   `load_state[key] = Error` and clears `pending_load`.
1849	
1850	## 6. Variant: Renamable Nodes
1851	
1852	`TreeView` supports inline rename of tree nodes, similar to file-explorer rename behavior.
```

## 3. Mapping to Core Component Contract

- Props parity: full parity with collection data, selected set, expanded set, selection behavior, and lazy-load or rename variants.
- State parity: full parity with focused node, expanded nodes, selected nodes, and focus-visible state.
- Part parity: full parity with `Root`, repeated `Branch`, `BranchControl`, `BranchIndicator`, `BranchText`, `BranchContent`, repeated `Leaf`, and `LeafText`.
- Adapter additions: explicit collection-backed rendering, live node registration, scroll-into-view sequencing, and `aria-owns` fallback when structure is not nested.

## 4. Part Mapping

| Core part / structure | Required?            | Adapter rendering target  | Ownership     | Attr source                       | Notes                                  |
| --------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `Root`                | required             | `<ul>` or `<div>`         | adapter-owned | `api.root_attrs()`                | owns tree role and descendant registry |
| `Branch`              | repeated             | `<li>` or `<div>`         | adapter-owned | `api.branch_attrs(key)`           | `role="treeitem"` with expand state    |

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/ericson/.claude/projects/-Users-ericson-Workspace-Rust-ars-ui/memory/feedback_adapter_notification_callbacks.md",
  "content": "---\nname: feedback_adapter_notification_callbacks\ndescription: Consumer/adapter notifications are Props Callback fired by a typed Effect closure; never Rc aliases or transient context fields\nmetadata:\n  type: feedback\n---\n\nIn ars-ui, a component's notifications to the consumer/adapter (selection changed, reorder, lazy-load-children, etc.) are modeled as a `Props` field `Option<Callback<dyn Fn(Args) + Send + Sync>>`, invoked from inside a **typed `Effect`'s closure** (`PendingEffect::new(Effect::X, move |_ctx, props, _send| { if let Some(cb) = &props.on_x { cb(captured_args) } no_cleanup() })`). The payload is **captured by the effect closure**, not carried on the `Effect` enum variant (`Machine::Effect: EffectName` requires `Copy`, so variants stay unit-like) and not stashed in a transient `Context` field for the adapter to read.\n\n**Why:** `Callback<T>` wraps `Arc<T>` (thread-safe — the `Service` lives in Leptos `StoredValue` / Dioxus `Signal`, which require `Send + Sync`). `Rc<dyn Fn(..)>` is `!Send`/`!Sync` and breaks that. A transient `Context` field (e.g. `pending_load`) is redundant noise when the closure can capture the value — and it's inconsistent with how `on_selection_change`/`on_expanded_change`/`on_reorder` already work. The `ScrollFocusedIntoView`-reads-`focused_node` pattern is only for data that is *already* persistent context, not for payloads that exist solely to reach the adapter.\n\n**How to apply:** When a spec (often a stale variant section) defines an adapter callback as `pub type FooFn = Rc<dyn Fn(..)>` \"registered in the adapter, not in Props,\" treat that as drift. Implement it as a real `on_foo: Option<Callback<dyn Fn(..) + Send + Sync>>` Prop with a builder, fired by a typed `Effect::Foo` closure, mirroring the sibling callbacks. Surfaced on the TreeView §5 lazy-load `LoadChildren` work (2026-05-27). Relates to [[feedback_messagefn_send_sync]], [[feedback_no_namespacing_in_struct_names]].\n"
}

The branch key is\n  captured by the effect's closure; no transient \\`Context\\` field\n  carries it. The original spec defined a \\`Rc<dyn Fn(Key)>\\` alias\n  registered \\\"in the adapter, not in Props\\\" — that was stale (not\n  \\`Send + Sync\\` for the workspace's threaded \\`Service\\` storage, and\n  inconsistent with the sibling callbacks); the canonical model is\n  Props-Callback fired by a typed Effect.\n* Events: \\`ChildrenLoaded { parent, children: Vec<TreeItemConfig<TreeItem>> }\\`\n  splices the loaded configs in under \\`parent\\` and reseeds\n  \\`load_state\\` so \\`parent\\` flips to \\`Loaded\\`. \\`LoadError(Key)\\` marks\n  the node \\`Error\\`. A \\`NotLoaded\\` re-expand retries; \\`Loaded\\`/\\`Error\\`\n  branches do not silently re-trigger.\n* A loading branch advertises \\`aria-busy=\\\"true\\\"\\` and\n  \\`data-ars-loading\\` on its branch/leaf element.\n* API: \\`node_load_state\\`/\\`is_loading\\` accessors; \\`on_load_children\\`\n  builder.\n\n§6 Renamable Nodes\n* \\`Props::renamable: bool\\` (default false) + builder.\n* \\`Context::renaming_key: Option<Key>\\` (init None; cleared on\n  \\`SyncProps\\` when the renaming node is no longer in the collection).\n* Events: \\`RenameStart(Key)\\` is gated on \\`renamable\\` + node enabled +\n  state Idle/Focused, and retargets if another node is already\n  renaming; \\`RenameCommit { key, new_name }\\` / \\`RenameCancel(Key)\\`\n  clear \\`renaming_key\\` (guarded to the matching key).\n* New \\`Part::NodeRenameInput { node_id: Key }\\` (declared between\n  \\`LeafText\\` and \\`DragHandle\\`); \\`node_rename_input_attrs\\` renders\n  \\`type=text\\`, \\`value=label\\`, \\`aria-label\\` from\n  \\`Messages::rename_label\\` (new \\`MessageFn<RenameLabelFn>\\` defaulting\n  to \\`|node_name, _| format!(\\\"Rename {node_name}\\\")\\`).\n* API: \\`is_renaming\\`, \\`on_rename_input_keydown\\` (Enter ->\n  RenameCommit, Escape -> RenameCancel), \\`on_rename_input_blur\\`\n  (commits if still active). \\`F2\\` on a node dispatches \\`RenameStart\\`.\n\nCross-cutting\n* \\`TreeItemConfig\\` in \\`ars-collections\\` now derives\n  \\`Clone, PartialEq\\` (gated on \\`T\\`) so it can ride inside the\n  \\`ChildrenLoaded\\` event variant (which requires \\`Clone + PartialEq\\`).\n  \\`Debug\\` remains hand-written to avoid a \\`T: Debug\\` bound.\n* TreeView \\`Event::FocusNext\\`/\\`FocusPrev\\` doc comments wrongly said\n  \\\"wraps to the first/last\\\" — corrected to \\\"(does not wrap)\\\". ----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Load every lazy branch expanded by ExpandAll**

When `Event::ExpandAll` passes all newly expanded keys into `expanded_change_plan`, this `.find()` selects only the first `NotLoaded` branch to mark `Loading` and attach a `LoadChildren` effect. In a tree with multiple lazy branches, the remaining branches are inserted into the expanded set while staying `NotLoaded`, so they render as expanded empty branches and never call `on_load_children` unless the user later collapses and re-expands each one. The lazy-loading contract says a `NotLoaded` node emits `LoadChildren` when it is first expanded, so this should schedule a load for each lazy key expanded by the bulk action.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

========================================
THREAD id=PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FSSSA
  path=crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs line=1208
  comment_db_id=3315181284
----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Notify consumers when a rename is committed**

For the renamable variant, Enter and blur send `RenameCommit { key, new_name }`, but the transition discards `new_name` and only clears `renaming_key`; there is also no `Props` callback or effect carrying the committed value. In any app using inline rename, the consumer therefore has no way to observe the new label and update the backing `TreeCollection`, so the edit disappears on the next render despite the spec saying the consumer persists the new name.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

========================================
THREAD id=PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FSSSC
  path=crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs line=352
  comment_db_id=3315181286
----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear active rename when disabling renamable**

This new prop can change from `true` to `false` while a node is being edited, but `Machine::on_props_changed` does not include `renamable` and `is_renaming()` only checks `ctx.renaming_key`. In that scenario the service props say renaming is disabled, yet the existing `renaming_key` remains live and adapters following the spec continue to render `NodeRenameInput` until the user commits or cancels; the prop change should trigger sync/clear or the API should gate rendering on the current prop.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

========================================
THREAD id=PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FSSSE
  path=crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs line=1155
  comment_db_id=3315181288
----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore stale ChildrenLoaded deliveries**

`ChildrenLoaded` unconditionally rebuilds the collection with the delivered children whenever the parent key exists. If a load completion is delivered twice, or an old async completion arrives after the parent has already been populated by props/a previous completion, `insert_loaded_children` appends the same child configs again; `TreeCollection::new` allows duplicate nodes while `get()` points at only the last duplicate, leaving duplicated visible rows and inconsistent key lookups. This event should be accepted only for the in-flight lazy-load state, or should replace the unloaded child set instead of appending to an already-loaded parent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD id=PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FSSSI
  path=crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs line=1749
  comment_db_id=3315181292
----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow retry after lazy-load errors**

After `LoadError(key)` sets a lazy branch to `Error`, subsequent `ExpandNode`/`ToggleNode` calls can never emit another `LoadChildren` effect because this predicate only treats `NotLoaded` as loadable, and there is no other public event that resets `Error` or requests a retry. In the failure path described by the new lazy-loading variant, an adapter may show a retry affordance, but invoking the normal expand path leaves the branch stuck in `Error` indefinitely unless the consumer rebuilds props out-of-band.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "old_string": "/// Lazy loading (spec §5): `expanding` lists the keys this event is expanding\n/// (empty for collapses). The first such key whose [`NodeLoadState`] is\n/// `NotLoaded` triggers a lazy load — it is marked `Loading` and an\n/// [`Effect::LoadChildren`] carrying that key is attached, which invokes\n/// [`Props::on_load_children`]. This fires regardless of the\n/// controlled/uncontrolled split (the load is needed before any echo can produce\n/// children) and even when the expansion set is unchanged (re-expanding a\n/// still-`NotLoaded` branch retries the load).\nfn expanded_change_plan(\n    ctx: &Context,\n    next: BTreeSet<Key>,\n    clamp: bool,\n    expanding: &[Key],\n) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let unchanged = ctx.expanded.get() == &next;\n\n    // The first branch this event expands that still awaits a lazy load.\n    let lazy = expanding\n        .iter()\n        .find(|key| needs_lazy_load(ctx, key))\n        .cloned();\n\n    // Nothing to do when neither the expansion set nor a load needs to change.\n    if unchanged && lazy.is_none() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let effect = expanded_change_effect(next.clone());\n\n    let mut plan = if ctx.expanded.is_controlled() {\n        TransitionPlan::new().apply(|_: &mut Context| {})\n    } else {\n        TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n            ctx.expanded.set(next);\n            if clamp {\n                clamp_focus_to_visible(ctx);\n            }\n        })\n    };\n\n    // Only attach the expanded-change notification when the set actually\n    // changed; a pure lazy-load retrigger does not move the expansion set.\n    if !unchanged {\n        plan = plan.with_effect(effect);\n    }\n\n    if let Some(key) = lazy {\n        let request = key.clone();\n        plan = plan\n            .apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                ctx.load_state.insert(key.clone(), NodeLoadState::Loading);\n            })\n            .with_effect(load_children_effect(request));\n    }\n\n    Some(plan)\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Lazy loading (spec §5): `expanding` lists the keys this event is expanding\n/// (empty for collapses). Every key in `expanding` whose [`NodeLoadState`] is\n/// `NotLoaded` (or `Error`, for retry) triggers a lazy load — each such key is\n/// marked `Loading` and a dedicated [`Effect::LoadChildren`] carrying its key\n/// is attached, which invokes [`Props::on_load_children`]. The bulk path\n/// (`ExpandAll`) therefore fans one load per lazy branch instead of stranding\n/// the rest as expanded-but-empty. Loads fire regardless of the\n/// controlled/uncontrolled split (the load is needed before any echo can\n/// produce children) and even when the expansion set is unchanged (re-expanding\n/// a still-`NotLoaded`/`Error` branch retries the load).\nfn expanded_change_plan(\n    ctx: &Context,\n    next: BTreeSet<Key>,\n    clamp: bool,\n    expanding: &[Key],\n) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let unchanged = ctx.expanded.get() == &next;\n\n    // Every branch this event expands that still awaits a lazy load.\n    let lazy: Vec<Key> = expanding\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|key| needs_lazy_load(ctx, key))\n        .cloned()\n        .collect();\n\n    // Nothing to do when neither the expansion set nor a load needs to change.\n    if unchanged && lazy.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let effect = expanded_change_effect(next.clone());\n\n    let mut plan = if ctx.expanded.is_controlled() {\n        TransitionPlan::new().apply(|_: &mut Context| {})\n    } else {\n        TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n            ctx.expanded.set(next);\n            if clamp {\n                clamp_focus_to_visible(ctx);\n            }\n        })\n    };\n\n    // Only attach the expanded-change notification when the set actually\n    // changed; a pure lazy-load retrigger does not move the expansion set.\n    if !unchanged {\n        plan = plan.with_effect(effect);\n    }\n\n    if !lazy.is_empty() {\n        let to_mark = lazy.clone();\n        plan = plan.apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n            for key in &to_mark {\n                ctx.load_state.insert(key.clone(), NodeLoadState::Loading);\n            }\n        });\n        for key in lazy {\n            plan = plan.with_effect(load_children_effect(key));\n        }\n    }\n\n    Some(plan)\n}"
}

1841	## 6. Variant: Renamable Nodes
1842	
1843	`TreeView` supports inline rename of tree nodes, similar to file-explorer rename behavior.
1844	When enabled, users can start renaming a node via F2 or slow double-click. The node's text
1845	display is replaced by an inline `<input>` element until the rename is committed or cancelled.
1846

1888	### 6.4 Behavior
1889	
1890	- **`RenameStart(key)`**: Only allowed from `Idle` or `Focused` states, and only for a real
1891	  node. If `renamable` is false or the target node is disabled, the event is ignored. If
1892	  another node is currently being renamed (`renaming_key` is `Some(other_key)`), the machine
1893	  simply retargets `renaming_key` to `Some(key)` and moves focus to the new input — the
1894	  previous rename is committed by the adapter's blur handler (`on_rename_input_blur`), which
1895	  fires `RenameCommit` for the outgoing input with its live DOM value as focus leaves it. The
1896	  agnostic core cannot read that DOM value, so the commit-previous behavior is driven by the
1897	  adapter rather than synthesized in the transition.
1898	- **`RenameCommit { key, new_name }`**: Clears `renaming_key` to `None`. The consumer is
1899	  responsible for persisting the new name (e.g., updating the `TreeCollection` data source).
1900	  The machine does not modify the `TreeItem.label` — the consumer updates the collection and
1901	  passes new props.
1902	- **`RenameCancel(key)`**: Clears `renaming_key` to `None`. No value change occurs. Focus
1903	  returns to the tree item that was being renamed.

  "old_string": "1. User expands a node whose `load_state` is `NotLoaded`.\n2. The machine sets `load_state[key] = Loading` and attaches an\n   `Effect::LoadChildren` whose closure captures `key` (in addition to the\n   normal expand plan).\n3. The adapter runs the effect, which invokes `Props::on_load_children(key)`.\n   The consumer fetches data asynchronously.\n4. Consumer sends `ChildrenLoaded { parent, children }` when data arrives.\n5. The machine splices the children in under `parent`, rebuilds the collection,\n   and reseeds `load_state` (so `parent` becomes `Loaded`).\n6. If loading fails, the consumer sends `LoadError(key)`; the machine sets\n   `load_state[key] = Error`.",
  "new_string": "1. User expands one or more nodes whose `load_state` is `NotLoaded` (or\n   previously failed `Error`).\n2. The machine sets `load_state[key] = Loading` for **every** such key in the\n   expanding set and attaches a dedicated `Effect::LoadChildren` per key (each\n   effect's closure captures its own key). Bulk paths (`ExpandAll`) therefore\n   fan one load per lazy branch instead of stranding the rest as expanded but\n   empty.\n3. The adapter runs each effect, which invokes `Props::on_load_children(key)`.\n   The consumer fetches data asynchronously.\n4. Consumer sends `ChildrenLoaded { parent, children }` when data arrives. The\n   machine accepts the delivery only when `load_state[parent] == Loading`;\n   stale or duplicate deliveries (e.g., a late async completion after another\n   load already finished, or a double-fire from the adapter) are dropped so\n   `TreeCollection` cannot accumulate duplicated rows.\n5. The machine splices the children in under `parent`, rebuilds the collection,\n   and reseeds `load_state` (so `parent` becomes `Loaded`).\n6. If loading fails, the consumer sends `LoadError(key)`; the machine sets\n   `load_state[key] = Error`. Re-expanding an `Error` branch retries the load\n   (the gate accepts both `NotLoaded` and `Error`), so an adapter retry\n   affordance only needs to re-dispatch `ExpandNode`/`ToggleNode` — no\n   separate retry event is required."
}

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve lazy-loaded children during prop sync**

When a branch is populated via `Event::ChildrenLoaded`, the loaded children live only in `ctx.items`; the stored `props.items` can still be the original lazy tree. On the next `SyncProps` for an unrelated prop change such as controlled `selected`, `expanded`, `id`, or `renamable`, `items_changed` becomes true because `ctx.items` includes the inserted children while `props.items` does not, and the sync path assigns `ctx.items = items` before reseeding here. That drops the already-loaded subtree and resets its state back to `NotLoaded`, so lazy children can disappear after any later controlled prop echo unless every consumer also mirrors the loaded children into props.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

========================================
THREAD id=PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FSelH
  path=crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs line=1106
  comment_db_id=3315250119
----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cancel rename when the node becomes disabled**

If a user starts renaming an enabled node and then a prop/data update changes that same `TreeItem` to `disabled: true`, this sync path preserves `renaming_key` because it only clears the target when the node is removed. The adapter will keep rendering `NodeRenameInput`, and a later blur/Enter still emits `Effect::Rename`, even though the rest of this machine treats disabled nodes as blocking all interaction (`RenameStart`, expand, drag, selection). Clear the active rename when the surviving target is now disabled as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

========================================
THREAD id=PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FSelK
  path=crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs line=1227
  comment_db_id=3315250123
----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore stale load failures after success**

A `LoadError` can arrive after the same async request has already delivered `ChildrenLoaded`; in that case the parent is no longer `Loading` and may already have visible children. This branch still overwrites the node's state to `Error`, so a late failure callback can make an already-loaded branch look failed and cause later expand/retry paths to request loading again. Mirror the `ChildrenLoaded` guard and only accept failures while the node is still in the in-flight `Loading` state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "            Event::LoadError(key) => {\n                // Only a tracked node can transition to `Error`.\n                ctx.items.get(key)?;\n\n                // Ignore stale failures: only accept `LoadError` while the\n                // node is in the in-flight `Loading` state, mirroring the\n                // `ChildrenLoaded` guard. Otherwise a late failure arriving\n                // after a successful load (or after a retry already\n                // resolved) would flip an already-`Loaded` branch back to\n                // `Error` and let the retry path request loading again.\n                if ctx.load_state.get(key) != Some(&NodeLoadState::Loading) {\n                    return None;\n                }\n\n                let key = key.clone();\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                    ctx.load_state.insert(key.clone(), NodeLoadState::Error);\n                }))\n            }"
}

1921	### 6.4 Behavior
1922	
1923	- **`RenameStart(key)`**: Only allowed from `Idle` or `Focused` states, and only for a real
1924	  node. If `renamable` is false or the target node is disabled, the event is ignored. If
1925	  another node is currently being renamed (`renaming_key` is `Some(other_key)`), the machine
1926	  simply retargets `renaming_key` to `Some(key)` and moves focus to the new input — the
1927	  previous rename is committed by the adapter's blur handler (`on_rename_input_blur`), which
1928	  fires `RenameCommit` for the outgoing input with its live DOM value as focus leaves it. The
1929	  agnostic core cannot read that DOM value, so the commit-previous behavior is driven by the
1930	  adapter rather than synthesized in the transition.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebuild disabled keys after lazy children load**

When a lazy load returns children with `TreeItem { disabled: true, .. }`, this path inserts those nodes into `ctx.items` but leaves `ctx.selection_state.disabled_keys` from the pre-load tree. `SelectNode` only checks that the key exists and is focusable before calling `selection_state.select`, so newly loaded disabled children can still become selected until a full props data-source change reseeds the selection state. Recompute the disabled-key set and selection state from the updated `ctx.items` after splicing children.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve blur commits after retargeting rename**

If a rename is active and another node starts renaming before the old input's blur handler runs, `RenameStart` retargets `renaming_key` to the new node first; then this blur helper sees that the old node is no longer `is_renaming` and drops the old input value. That loses the user's edit in the exact handoff the surrounding rename logic relies on blur to commit, so the blur path needs to be able to commit the outgoing node rather than gating solely on the current target.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve loaded children’s default expansion**

When `ChildrenLoaded` inserts a subtree containing a child branch with `default_expanded: true`, `TreeCollection::new` records that branch as expanded internally, but rendering and visibility are driven by `ctx.expanded` (`visible_keys_with_expanded(ctx.expanded.get())` and `is_node_expanded`). This closure replaces `ctx.items` without merging those newly inserted default-expanded keys into the uncontrolled expansion binding, so the loaded descendants render collapsed even though the delivered configs asked to start expanded.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve completed status across prop sync**

After the last-step completion path sets the current step's status to `Complete`, the active `step` still points at that same index. Any later unrelated `SyncProps` path that preserves runtime statuses calls `normalized_statuses(..., target)`, which forces the target index back to `Status::Current`, so toggling props such as `orientation` or `linear` immediately erases the completed state. Completion needs a separate persisted marker or a sync path that does not re-normalize the final completed step back to current.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let ToggleNode retry failed lazy loads**

After a lazy load fails, the branch remains expanded with `load_state == Error`; this `ToggleNode` arm treats that as a collapse and passes an empty `expanding` list, so it never emits `LoadChildren`. The spec says an adapter retry affordance can re-dispatch `ExpandNode`/`ToggleNode`, and the default branch control click uses `ToggleNode`, so retrying from an expanded error branch currently takes a collapse plus a second expand instead of actually retrying. Include `Error` branches in the toggle retry path before collapsing, or document that only `ExpandNode` retries.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "fn normalize_current_status(statuses: &mut [Status], current: u32) {\n    for (index, status) in statuses.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n        if index as u32 == current {\n            // Preserve `Complete` on the active index. The last-step\n            // completion path (spec §1.5: NextStep past the final step marks\n            // it `Complete`) must survive unrelated `SyncProps` echoes (e.g.\n            // toggling `orientation` or `linear`) — otherwise re-normalizing\n            // the active index back to `Current` quietly erases the\n            // completed-all-steps state. A status that is anything else\n            // (Incomplete/Error) at the active index still becomes Current.\n            if *status != Status::Complete {\n                *status = Status::Current;\n            }\n        } else if *status == Status::Current {\n            *status = Status::Incomplete;\n        }\n    }\n}"
}

{

  "old_string": "fn rename_commit_ignored_for_non_renaming_key() {\n    let mut service = service(renamable_props());\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::RenameStart(key(2))));\n\n    let result = service.send(Event::RenameCommit {\n        key: key(3),\n        new_name: \"x\".to_string(),\n    });\n\n    assert!(!result.context_changed);\n    assert_eq!(service.context().renaming_key, Some(key(2)));\n}",
  "new_string": "fn rename_commit_for_outgoing_key_still_fires_effect() {\n    // During a rename retarget the outgoing input's blur fires\n    // `RenameCommit` for the previous key while `renaming_key` already\n    // points at the new node. The transition must still emit\n    // `Effect::Rename` so the outgoing edit reaches the consumer; only the\n    // `renaming_key` clear is gated on the key actually being the active\n    // target.\n    let mut service = service(renamable_props());\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::RenameStart(key(2))));\n\n    let result = service.send(Event::RenameCommit {\n        key: key(3),\n        new_name: \"x\".to_string(),\n    });\n\n    // `renaming_key` is unchanged — the new active target stays.\n    assert_eq!(service.context().renaming_key, Some(key(2)));\n\n    // ...but `Effect::Rename` did fire for the committed (outgoing) key, so\n    // the consumer's `on_rename` receives the outgoing edit.\n    assert!(\n        result\n            .pending_effects\n            .iter()\n            .any(|effect| effect.name == Effect::Rename),\n        \"RenameCommit for an outgoing key still emits Effect::Rename\"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn rename_commit_no_op_when_no_rename_active() {\n    // A stray `RenameCommit` when nothing is renaming anywhere must be a\n    // pure no-op — no context change, no effect fired. Distinct from the\n    // retarget hand-off above (where a rename IS active on another key).\n    let mut service = service(renamable_props());\n\n    let result = service.send(Event::RenameCommit {\n        key: key(2),\n        new_name: \"x\".to_string(),\n    });\n\n    assert!(!result.context_changed);\n    assert!(result.pending_effects.is_empty());\n    assert_eq!(service.context().renaming_key, None);\n}"
}

  "new_string": "    assert_eq!(&items_after, &service.context().items);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn children_loaded_recomputes_disabled_keys_for_loaded_disabled_child() {\n    // A lazy load can deliver children carrying `TreeItem { disabled: true }`.\n    // `ChildrenLoaded` must rebuild `selection_state.disabled_keys` from the\n    // updated collection — otherwise `SelectNode` happily admits a key whose\n    // node is now disabled (the selection machine still trusts a stale\n    // disabled set).\n    let mut service = service(lazy_props());\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::ExpandNode(key(1))));\n    drop(service.send(Event::ChildrenLoaded {\n        parent: key(1),\n        children: vec![\n            leaf_with(\n                2,\n                \"Apple\",\n                TreeItem {\n                    disabled: true,\n                    ..item(\"Apple\")\n                },\n            ),\n            leaf(3, \"Banana\"),\n        ],\n    }));\n\n    // The disabled-key set now contains the newly-loaded disabled child.\n    assert!(service.context().selection_state.disabled_keys.contains(&key(2)));\n\n    // SelectNode on the disabled-but-loaded child is a no-op.\n    let before = service.context().selected.get().clone();\n    drop(service.send(Event::SelectNode(key(2))));\n    assert_eq!(&before, service.context().selected.get());\n\n    // The enabled sibling can still be selected.\n    drop(service.send(Event::SelectNode(key(3))));\n    assert!(service.context().selected.get().contains(&key(3)));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn children_loaded_seeds_default_expanded_for_loaded_subtree() {\n    // `TreeItemConfig::default_expanded: true` is honored at init via the\n    // initial `ctx.expanded` seeding. Lazy-load deliveries must honor it\n    // too — `TreeCollection::new` records the marker internally, but\n    // rendering is driven by `ctx.expanded`, so the descendant would\n    // render collapsed without an explicit merge.\n    let mut service = service(lazy_props());\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::ExpandNode(key(1))));\n    drop(service.send(Event::ChildrenLoaded {\n        parent: key(1),\n        children: vec![TreeItemConfig {\n            key: key(2),\n            text_value: \"Apple\".to_string(),\n            value: item(\"Apple\"),\n            children: vec![leaf(20, \"Apple Pie\")],\n            default_expanded: true,\n        }],\n    }));\n\n    let expanded = service.context().expanded.get();\n    assert!(\n        expanded.contains(&key(2)),\n        \"loaded child with default_expanded must be merged into ctx.expanded\"\n    );\n    assert!(service.connect(&|_| {}).is_node_expanded(&key(2)));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn blur_during_retarget_fires_rename_effect_for_outgoing_input() {\n    // Adapter contract: `on_rename_input_blur` fires `RenameCommit` for the\n    // outgoing input after a retarget, so the user's edit reaches\n    // `Props::on_rename` via `Effect::Rename`. The new active rename\n    // (`renaming_key = Some(other)`) is unaffected.\n    let captured: Arc<Mutex<Vec<RenameEvent>>> = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));\n    let sink = Arc::clone(&captured);\n\n    let mut service = service(\n        renamable_props().on_rename(move |event: RenameEvent| sink.lock().unwrap().push(event)),\n    );\n\n    // Start renaming node 2, then retarget to node 3 — `renaming_key` is now\n    // Some(key(3)) and node 2's input is the outgoing surface.\n    drop(service.send(Event::RenameStart(key(2))));\n    drop(service.send(Event::RenameStart(key(3))));\n    assert_eq!(service.context().renaming_key, Some(key(3)));\n\n    // Adapter dispatches the outgoing input's blur — through the API to\n    // verify the gate (must fire because `renaming_key.is_some()`).\n    let sent: Arc<Mutex<Vec<Event>>> = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));\n    let sent_clone = Arc::clone(&sent);\n    service\n        .connect(&move |event| sent_clone.lock().unwrap().push(event))\n        .on_rename_input_blur(&key(2), \"Apricot\");\n\n    let outgoing_event = sent\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .iter()\n        .find_map(|event| match event {\n            Event::RenameCommit { key, new_name } => Some((key.clone(), new_name.clone())),\n            _ => None,\n        })\n        .expect(\"blur during retarget must dispatch RenameCommit for the outgoing key\");\n    assert_eq!(outgoing_event, (key(2), \"Apricot\".to_string()));\n\n    // Replay the event through the service so the effect surface materializes.\n    let mut result = service.send(Event::RenameCommit {\n        key: key(2),\n        new_name: \"Apricot\".to_string(),\n    });\n\n    // Active rename target is unchanged.\n    assert_eq!(service.context().renaming_key, Some(key(3)));\n\n    // ...but Effect::Rename fired; running it delivers the outgoing edit.\n    let index = result\n        .pending_effects\n        .iter()\n        .position(|effect| effect.name == Effect::Rename)\n        .expect(\"retargeted RenameCommit emits Effect::Rename\");\n    let effect = result.pending_effects.remove(index);\n    let noop_send: StrongSend<Event> = Arc::new(|_| {});\n    drop(effect.run(service.context(), service.props(), noop_send));\n\n    assert_eq!(\n        captured.lock().unwrap().as_slice(),\n        &[RenameEvent {\n            key: key(2),\n            new_name: \"Apricot\".to_string(),\n        }]\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn toggle_node_on_error_branch_retries_load() {\n    // After a lazy load fails, the branch sits expanded with `Error` state.\n    // Adapter retry affordances re-dispatch `ToggleNode` (the default\n    // branch-control click path); the toggle must treat an `Error` branch\n    // as a retry rather than collapsing it, otherwise retrying requires a\n    // collapse + re-expand instead of one click.\n    let mut service = service(lazy_props());\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::ExpandNode(key(1))));\n    drop(service.send(Event::LoadError(key(1))));\n    assert_eq!(\n        service.connect(&|_| {}).node_load_state(&key(1)),\n        NodeLoadState::Error\n    );\n    assert!(service.connect(&|_| {}).is_node_expanded(&key(1)));\n\n    let result = service.send(Event::ToggleNode(key(1)));\n\n    // Branch stays expanded (retry, not collapse) and re-fires LoadChildren.\n    assert!(service.connect(&|_| {}).is_node_expanded(&key(1)));\n    assert_eq!(\n        service.connect(&|_| {}).node_load_state(&key(1)),\n        NodeLoadState::Loading\n    );\n    assert!(\n        result\n            .pending_effects\n            .iter()\n            .any(|effect| effect.name == Effect::LoadChildren),\n        \"ToggleNode on an Error branch must re-fire LoadChildren\"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn rename_input_snapshot() {"

Any later unrelated `SyncProps` (e.g. toggling\n        // `orientation`/`linear`) must preserve that completion — otherwise\n        // re-normalizing the active index back to `Current` quietly erases\n        // the \"all steps done\" state.\n        let mut service = service(props().default_step(3));\n\n        drop(service.send(Event::NextStep));\n        assert_eq!(service.context().statuses[3], Status::Complete);\n\n        // Unrelated prop echo: flip `orientation`.\n        let new_props = props().default_step(3).orientation(Orientation::Vertical);\n        let triggered =\n            <Machine as ars_core::Machine>::on_props_changed(service.props(), &new_props);\n        assert!(triggered.contains(&Event::SyncProps));\n\n        drop(service.set_props(new_props));\n        for event in triggered {\n            drop(service.send(event));\n        }\n\n        // Completion survives the echo.\n        assert_eq!(service.context().statuses[3], Status::Complete);\n        assert_eq!(*service.context().step.get(), 3);\n    }"

1950	  toggle as a sync trigger; the resulting `SyncProps` arm clears `renaming_key` when the live

All 5 round-3 fixes are in the working tree with TDD coverage:

- **R3-T1** (rebuild `disabled_keys` after `ChildrenLoaded`) + **R3-T3** (merge loaded `default_expanded`): both folded into the `ChildrenLoaded` apply closure with a new `collect_default_expanded` helper. Test: a newly-loaded disabled child cannot be selected; a `default_expanded` config sub-config merges into `ctx.expanded`.
- **R3-T2** (preserve outgoing-key blur during rename retarget): relaxed both the `on_rename_input_blur` API gate (`renaming_key.is_some()`) and the `RenameCommit` transition gate (rejects only when no rename is active anywhere); `renaming_key` clear remains gated on key match. Renamed the existing over-strict test + added a new test using the API end-to-end.
- **R3-T4** (Steps last-step completion survives `SyncProps` echo): scoped the fix to the SyncProps preserve-path (not `normalize_current_status` globally) so navigation back to a completed step still flips it to `Current` — only the post-completion echo preserves `Complete`. New Steps test.
- **R3-T5** (`ToggleNode` retries failed lazy loads): on `Error` state, toggle expands+loads instead of collapsing. New test.

569 nav lib tests pass, clippy `-D warnings` clean, spec validate + snippet-compile pass. `xci-fast` running for the final gate; I'll commit + push + reply + resolve + re-trigger Codex on confirm.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept retargeted rename commits in the spec snippet**

This pseudo-code still rejects `RenameCommit` whenever `renaming_key` has already moved to another node, which contradicts the §6.4 retarget hand-off described just above and the implementation/tests in `tree_view::Machine`: after starting rename on B while A's input blurs, the outgoing `RenameCommit { key: A, ... }` must still emit `Effect::Rename` without clearing B's active rename. Leaving this snippet as-is would make spec-driven adapter/core implementations silently drop the user's edit in that retarget scenario.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute disabled keys from preserved lazy items**

When a lazy load inserts a disabled child and a later unrelated prop echo hits `SyncProps` without changing `Props::items`, this new `items_changed == false` path keeps the loaded subtree in `ctx.items`, but `disabled_keys` was already computed from the stale prop collection above. The subsequent `sanitize_selection`/`with_disabled(disabled_keys)` then forgets that the loaded child is disabled, so a following `SelectNode` can select a node that `ChildrenLoaded` had correctly marked non-selectable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

When a\n    // rename IS active — either for `key` or (during the retarget hand-off,\n    // see §6.4 prose above) for a different node — emit `Effect::Rename`\n    // so the outgoing edit reaches `Props::on_rename`. The `renaming_key`\n    // clear is gated on the key actually being the current target, so a\n    // retargeted blur commits the outgoing value without ending the new\n    // node's rename.\n    ctx.renaming_key.as_ref()?;\n    let event = RenameEvent { key: key.clone(), new_name: new_name.clone() };\n    let is_active_target = ctx.renaming_key.as_ref() == Some(key);\n    Some(\n        TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n            if is_active_target {\n                ctx.renaming_key = None;\n            }\n        })\n        .with_effect(rename_effect(event)),"

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid optimistic completion in controlled steps**

When `Props::step` is controlled and the user advances past the last step, this new path still mutates `ctx.statuses` before firing `on_complete`. Other navigation goes through `step_change_plan`, which returns without mutating context for controlled step state, so a parent that keeps the controlled step/statuses unchanged or rejects completion will briefly render the final step as `Complete` anyway until a prop echo corrects it. Please keep this path consistent with controlled navigation by only notifying in controlled mode and letting the parent echo the completed status.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

========================================
THREAD id=PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FTMvN
  path=spec/components/navigation/accordion.md line=173
  comment_db_id=3315508551
----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the unspecified future state**

In this component spec, calling out an `Animating` state as a “potential future extension” violates the repo's spec rule that forbids deferral language and requires every mentioned feature to be fully specified. As written, the spec now names an undefined state that implementers could treat as part of the intended contract without any transitions, accessibility behavior, or tests to follow; either specify it fully here or remove the future-state example.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

========================================
THREAD id=PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FTMvP
  path=crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs line=1260
  comment_db_id=3315508553
----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject duplicate lazy-loaded keys before splicing**

When a `ChildrenLoaded` payload contains a key that already exists elsewhere in the tree, or duplicates a key within the loaded children, this call rebuilds the collection without validation. `TreeCollection::new` silently allows duplicate rows while its key lookup points at the last occurrence, so one bad lazy-load response can leave focus, selection, and ARIA ids resolving to a different row than the duplicate visible item. Please validate the incoming subtree keys against the current collection and each other before inserting.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "old_string": "/// Walk a [`TreeItemConfig`] subtree and accumulate every key whose config\n/// asked to start expanded. Used by [`Event::ChildrenLoaded`] to merge a\n/// lazy-loaded subtree's `default_expanded` markers into the runtime\n/// expansion binding, so descendants render expanded the way the configs\n/// requested (mirroring the init-time seeding from\n/// [`TreeItemConfig::default_expanded`]).\nfn collect_default_expanded(config: &TreeItemConfig<TreeItem>, expanded: &mut BTreeSet<Key>) {",
  "new_string": "/// Returns `true` when every key in the loaded `children` forest is unique\n/// across the forest itself **and** absent from the current `items`\n/// collection. `TreeCollection::new` accepts duplicate nodes silently and\n/// resolves `get()` to the last occurrence only, so a lazy-load payload\n/// with a duplicated key would leave focus / selection / ARIA ids\n/// pointing at a different row than the visible duplicate — making it a\n/// hard-to-trace data corruption. Used as a [`Event::ChildrenLoaded`]\n/// transition-time guard before splicing.\nfn loaded_keys_are_unique(\n    items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>,\n    children: &[TreeItemConfig<TreeItem>],\n) -> bool {\n    fn walk(\n        config: &TreeItemConfig<TreeItem>,\n        items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>,\n        seen: &mut BTreeSet<Key>,\n    ) -> bool {\n        if items.get(&config.key).is_some() {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        if !seen.insert(config.key.clone()) {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        for child in &config.children {\n            if !walk(child, items, seen) {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n\n        true\n    }\n\n    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();\n\n    for root in children {\n        if !walk(root, items, &mut seen) {\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    true\n}\n\n/// Walk a [`TreeItemConfig`] subtree and accumulate every key whose config\n/// asked to start expanded. Used by [`Event::ChildrenLoaded`] to merge a\n/// lazy-loaded subtree's `default_expanded` markers into the runtime\n/// expansion binding, so descendants render expanded the way the configs\n/// requested (mirroring the init-time seeding from\n/// [`TreeItemConfig::default_expanded`]).\nfn collect_default_expanded(config: &TreeItemConfig<TreeItem>, expanded: &mut BTreeSet<Key>) {"
}

  "new_string": "        // Completion survives the echo.\n        assert_eq!(service.context().statuses[3], Status::Complete);\n        assert_eq!(*service.context().step.get(), 3);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn controlled_last_step_completion_only_notifies() {\n        // In controlled-step mode the parent owns the step state, so the\n        // last-step completion path is notify-only (matches the controlled\n        // split used by `step_change_plan`): `statuses[active]` must NOT be\n        // pre-mutated to `Complete` — the parent decides whether to echo the\n        // completed state via a next props update. Pre-mutating would\n        // briefly render the final step `Complete` before a parent that\n        // rejects completion echoed it back.\n        let completed = Arc::new(Mutex::new(0usize));\n        let completed_clone = Arc::clone(&completed);\n        let mut service = service(\n            Props::new()\n                .id(\"steps\")\n                .count(NonZeroU32::new(4).expect(\"non-zero\"))\n                .step(3) // controlled, sitting on the last step\n                .on_complete(move || *lock(&completed_clone) += 1),\n        );\n\n        assert_eq!(service.context().statuses[3], Status::Current);\n\n        let result = service.send(Event::NextStep);\n\n        // No optimistic mutation — controlled state stays pristine.\n        assert_eq!(service.context().statuses[3], Status::Current);\n\n        // `Effect::Complete` still fires so the consumer is notified.\n        assert_eq!(result.pending_effects.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(result.pending_effects[0].name, Effect::Complete);\n\n        let send: StrongSend<Event> = Arc::new(|_| {});\n        for effect in result.pending_effects {\n            drop(effect.run(service.context(), service.props(), Arc::clone(&send)));\n        }\n\n        assert_eq!(*lock(&completed), 1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn sync_props_preserves_runtime_statuses_when_status_prop_is_unchanged() {"
}

{

  "old_string": "    // SelectNode on the disabled-but-loaded child remains a no-op.\n    let before = service.context().selected.get().clone();\n    drop(service.send(Event::SelectNode(key(2))));\n    assert_eq!(&before, service.context().selected.get());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn children_loaded_seeds_default_expanded_for_loaded_subtree() {",
  "new_string": "    // SelectNode on the disabled-but-loaded child remains a no-op.\n    let before = service.context().selected.get().clone();\n    drop(service.send(Event::SelectNode(key(2))));\n    assert_eq!(&before, service.context().selected.get());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn children_loaded_rejects_payload_with_duplicate_keys() {\n    // `TreeCollection::new` silently accepts duplicate nodes while resolving\n    // `get()` to the last occurrence only, so a lazy-load payload with a\n    // duplicated key would leave focus / selection / ARIA ids pointing at a\n    // different row than the visible duplicate. The `ChildrenLoaded` arm\n    // rejects such payloads — both keys that collide with the existing\n    // collection AND keys that duplicate each other within the payload.\n\n    // Case A: loaded child collides with a key that already exists in the\n    // tree (`key(7)` \"Grains\" is a root sibling in `lazy_items`).\n    let mut service_a = service(lazy_props());\n    drop(service_a.send(Event::ExpandNode(key(1))));\n\n    let result_a = service_a.send(Event::ChildrenLoaded {\n        parent: key(1),\n        children: vec![leaf(7, \"Duplicate Grains\")],\n    });\n\n    assert!(\n        !result_a.context_changed,\n        \"ChildrenLoaded must reject a payload whose key already exists in items\"\n    );\n    // Parent stays `Loading` — the delivery was rejected, not consumed, so\n    // a retry / a corrected payload can still settle the load.\n    assert_eq!(\n        service_a.connect(&|_| {}).node_load_state(&key(1)),\n        NodeLoadState::Loading\n    );\n\n    // Case B: loaded children duplicate each other within the payload.\n    let mut service_b = service(lazy_props());\n    drop(service_b.send(Event::ExpandNode(key(1))));\n\n    let result_b = service_b.send(Event::ChildrenLoaded {\n        parent: key(1),\n        children: vec![leaf(2, \"Apple\"), leaf(2, \"Apple Twin\")],\n    });\n\n    assert!(\n        !result_b.context_changed,\n        \"ChildrenLoaded must reject a payload whose own keys duplicate each other\"\n    );\n    assert_eq!(\n        service_b.connect(&|_| {}).node_load_state(&key(1)),\n        NodeLoadState::Loading\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn children_loaded_seeds_default_expanded_for_loaded_subtree() {"
}

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark the final step complete even when `step` is controlled**

When only the active `step` prop is controlled and `statuses` is not provided, advancing from the last step now fires `on_complete` but leaves `ctx.statuses[current]` as `Current` because this branch skips the status mutation. The parent has no status-change callback to echo a completed status, so the rendered item remains `data-ars-state="current"` after completion instead of the spec's post-completion `Complete` state; controlled `step` should only prevent mutating the active index, not the internal status list.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

========================================
THREAD id=PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FTeWD
  path=crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs line=1276
  comment_db_id=3315613019
----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve other pending lazy-load states**

When multiple lazy branches are loading concurrently (for example after `ExpandAll` emits one `LoadChildren` effect per branch), settling the first branch with `ChildrenLoaded` reseeds the entire map and turns every other still-empty `Loading` branch back into `NotLoaded`. The later `ChildrenLoaded`/`LoadError` for those branches is then rejected by the `== Loading` guard, leaving expanded branches empty even though their fetch completed; update only the settled parent and newly inserted subtree, or preserve other existing `Loading`/`Error` entries.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

========================================
THREAD id=PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FTeWE
  path=crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs line=1360
  comment_db_id=3315613023
----------------------------------------
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject hidden nodes before starting inline rename**

When `RenameStart` is dispatched for a real node hidden under a collapsed ancestor (e.g. a stale adapter handler or direct event send), this sets `focused_node` to that hidden key even though no `NodeRenameInput` or treeitem is rendered for it. `root_attrs()` will then emit `aria-activedescendant` for an id that is not in the visible DOM; mirror the `FocusNode`/`DragStart` visibility guard before assigning the rename target and focus.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Used by\n/// [`Event::ChildrenLoaded`] instead of a full `seed_load_state` reset: a\n/// full reset would clobber other in-flight `Loading`/`Error` entries when\n/// multiple branches are lazy-loading concurrently (e.g. `ExpandAll` over\n/// several lazy branches), and the later deliveries would then be rejected\n/// by the `== Loading` guard against an entry that was silently reset to\n/// `NotLoaded`.\n///\n/// A child with the `TreeItem::has_children` affordance but no actual\n/// children in the delivered config is seeded `NotLoaded` (it itself is a\n/// lazy branch); every other newly-inserted node is `Loaded`.\nfn seed_load_state_for_loaded(\n    configs: &[TreeItemConfig<TreeItem>],\n    load_state: &mut BTreeMap<Key, NodeLoadState>,\n) {\n    for config in configs {\n        let lazy = config.value.has_children && config.children.is_empty();\n        let state = if lazy {\n            NodeLoadState::NotLoaded\n        } else {\n            NodeLoadState::Loaded\n        };\n        load_state.insert(config.key.clone(), state);\n        seed_load_state_for_loaded(&config.children, load_state);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Walk a [`TreeItemConfig`] subtree and accumulate every key whose config\n/// asked to start expanded. Used by [`Event::ChildrenLoaded`] to merge a\n/// lazy-loaded subtree's `default_expanded` markers into the runtime\n/// expansion binding, so descendants render expanded the way the configs\n/// requested (mirroring the init-time seeding from\n/// [`TreeItemConfig::default_expanded`]).\nfn collect_default_expanded(config: &TreeItemConfig<TreeItem>, expanded: &mut BTreeSet<Key>) {"

  "new_string": "        \"ToggleNode on an Error branch must re-fire LoadChildren\"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn concurrent_lazy_loads_preserve_other_loading_states_when_one_settles() {\n    // When `ExpandAll` (or any path) fires `LoadChildren` for multiple\n    // lazy branches concurrently, settling the first via `ChildrenLoaded`\n    // must NOT reset every other still-in-flight branch's `Loading` entry\n    // back to `NotLoaded` — the later deliveries would then be rejected by\n    // the `== Loading` stale-guard against the wrongly-reset entry,\n    // leaving expanded branches empty even after their fetch completed.\n    let items = TreeCollection::new(vec![\n        leaf_with(\n            1,\n            \"Fruits\",\n            TreeItem {\n                has_children: true,\n                ..item(\"Fruits\")\n            },\n        ),\n        leaf_with(\n            8,\n            \"Beverages\",\n            TreeItem {\n                has_children: true,\n                ..item(\"Beverages\")\n            },\n        ),\n    ]);\n    let mut service = service(Props::new().id(\"tree\").items(items));\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::ExpandAll));\n    assert_eq!(\n        service.connect(&|_| {}).node_load_state(&key(1)),\n        NodeLoadState::Loading\n    );\n    assert_eq!(\n        service.connect(&|_| {}).node_load_state(&key(8)),\n        NodeLoadState::Loading\n    );\n\n    // Settle the first lazy branch.\n    drop(service.send(Event::ChildrenLoaded {\n        parent: key(1),\n        children: vec![leaf(2, \"Apple\")],\n    }));\n\n    // The other branch still reports `Loading` — its pending fetch is\n    // preserved (this is the new contract; previously it would have flipped\n    // back to `NotLoaded` because a full reseed wiped it).\n    assert_eq!(\n        service.connect(&|_| {}).node_load_state(&key(1)),\n        NodeLoadState::Loaded\n    );\n    assert_eq!(\n        service.connect(&|_| {}).node_load_state(&key(8)),\n        NodeLoadState::Loading,\n        \"settling one branch must not wipe another branch's pending Loading state\"\n    );\n\n    // The later delivery for the other branch is accepted (the `== Loading`\n    // stale-guard would have rejected it if the state had been reset).\n    drop(service.send(Event::ChildrenLoaded {\n        parent: key(8),\n        children: vec![leaf(9, \"Tea\")],\n    }));\n    assert_eq!(\n        service.connect(&|_| {}).node_load_state(&key(8)),\n        NodeLoadState::Loaded\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn rename_start_rejected_for_node_hidden_under_collapsed_parent() {\n    // A hidden node (under a collapsed ancestor) has no rendered `treeitem`\n    // or `NodeRenameInput`, so accepting `RenameStart` for it would set\n    // `focused_node`/`aria-activedescendant` to an id absent from the DOM.\n    // Mirrors the `FocusNode` / `DragStart` visibility guards.\n    let mut service = service(renamable_props());\n\n    // `key(5)` \"Carrot\" lives under \"Vegetables\" (key 4), which is\n    // `default_expanded: false` in `sample_items`, so its children are\n    // not visible at init.\n    let result = service.send(Event::RenameStart(key(5)));\n\n    assert!(\n        !result.context_changed,\n        \"RenameStart on a hidden node must be rejected\"\n    );\n    assert_eq!(service.context().renaming_key, None);\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, None);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn rename_input_snapshot() {"

Round-6 fixes are in the working tree:

- **R6-T1** (Codex correctly pushed back on my R5-T1): the `controlled` gate I added was over-eager — `statuses` is machine-owned (not a `Bindable`), so the spec-mandated post-completion `Complete` marker must apply even when `step` is controlled. Reverted the gate; updated the R5-T1 test to assert the corrected (and originally-correct) behavior.
- **R6-T2** (preserve other pending lazy loads): replaced the full `seed_load_state(&ctx.items)` reset in `ChildrenLoaded` with a `seed_load_state_for_loaded` helper that seeds only the freshly-inserted subtree, leaving every other pending `Loading`/`Error` entry untouched. New TDD test `concurrent_lazy_loads_preserve_other_loading_states_when_one_settles` covers the ExpandAll-fans-N-loads scenario.
- **R6-T3** (visibility guard in `RenameStart`): mirrored `FocusNode`/`DragStart` — `RenameStart` now rejects a node hidden under a collapsed ancestor. New TDD test `rename_start_rejected_for_node_hidden_under_collapsed_parent`.

574 nav tests, clippy `-D warnings` clean, spec gates green. `xci-fast` running; on confirm I'll commit, push, reply on all 3 R6 threads, resolve, and re-trigger Codex.
